task: This is a synthetic writing exercise. Using these fictional reporting notes, write a newspaper news story for general readers. Draw only on the supplied notes; do not invent additional reported events, scenes, or quotations. Write from this reporting snapshot as of December 5, 2024. Include a headline. Target 450 to 650 words. Follow AP style.

facts.text: A federal geological survey published December 5, 2024, found the Meridian Plains Aquifer is declining at 1.54 meters per year, approximately 40% faster than the 1.1-meter annual rate estimated in the agency's 2015 assessment.
The aquifer underlies 2.8 million acres of irrigated farmland across four states and supplies drinking water to more than 400,000 rural residents.
Groundwater levels in the study area are already 18 meters below their 1990 baseline.
Lead hydrologist Dr. Sarah Kimani said: "The revised rate reflects both increased extraction and reduced natural recharge. Some portions of the aquifer won't recover on any human timescale."
The study used data from 1,200 monitoring wells over a nine-year period from 2015 to 2024.
Irrigation accounts for 91% of aquifer extraction; the remainder is from municipal and residential use.
At the current depletion rate, the survey estimates economically viable irrigation in the shallowest portions of the aquifer will end within 20 to 35 years in those zones.
Bruce Holt, president of the Meridian Plains Growers Association, said the survey overstates the extraction rate and called for an independent review of the monitoring well methodology.
The U.S. Department of Agriculture estimated that crops grown in the aquifer's service area produced $14.2 billion in farm sales in 2023.
Several states in the region have implemented extraction limits, but enforcement mechanisms vary and the limits are set by state water authorities rather than a coordinated federal program.
The aquifer's natural recharge rate — the speed at which precipitation replenishes it — averages 0.03 meters per year, less than 2% of the current extraction rate.
The survey found a 22% increase in the number of wells that reported declining yield between 2019 and 2024 compared to the previous five-year period.
Dryland farming — crops that require no irrigation — has expanded on roughly 8% of the study area over the past decade as some producers anticipate water scarcity.
Dr. Kimani said the agency will publish zone-specific depletion maps in early 2025 to give state water planners more granular data.
Some economists have proposed tradeable water rights markets as a mechanism to reduce total extraction; no state in the region has adopted such a system.
The Meridian Plains Aquifer was first systematically surveyed in the 1950s when large-scale irrigation expanded into the region.
Federal water assistance programs provide subsidized irrigation infrastructure; critics say the subsidies reduce the financial incentive to conserve.
At least three cities in the aquifer region are conducting feasibility studies for supplemental water sources, including pipeline imports and wastewater recycling.
The survey did not estimate when total aquifer exhaustion would occur, noting that depletion is uneven across the formation.
Holt did not dispute the overall direction of the trend but said the rate calculation relied on wells concentrated in heavily pumped areas, potentially skewing the estimate.

forbidden_additions: a specific year for aquifer exhaustion
a claim that the aquifer is already depleted in any zone
endorsement of any specific policy recommendation as the agency's conclusion
